entities.name: Henri de La Tour d'Auvergne, Duke of Bouillon
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Henri de La Tour d'Auvergne, Duke of Bouillon, was a prominent Huguenot leader in 17th-century France. A member of the powerful House of La Tour d'Auvergne, he played a key role in the French Wars of Religion, earning the respect of his peers and the ire of his Catholic adversaries. His military prowess and diplomatic skills allowed him to navigate the complex web of alliances and rivalries between French Protestant and Catholic factions.

As a marshal of France, Bouillon participated in several key battles, including the Battle of La Rochelle in 1627, where he helped repel a Catholic army. His leadership during this battle cemented his reputation as a skilled military commander and earned him the admiration of his contemporaries.

Despite his military successes, Bouillon's personal life was marked by tragedy. He lost his wife and children in a fire at their chateau in 1622, an event that would haunt him for the rest of his life. This personal loss likely contributed to his growing religiosity and further solidified his commitment to the Huguenot cause.

Bouillon's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as his actions and decisions had a lasting impact on French history. He played a key role in the development of the Huguenot movement, which would continue to shape French politics and society for centuries to come.

Henri de La Tour d'Auvergne, duc de Bouillon, died on March 25, 1623, at the age of 53, leaving behind a legacy of military bravery, diplomatic skill, and unwavering commitment to his faith.

In the annals of history, Bouillon's name stands as a testament to the enduring power of faith, family, and country. His story serves as a reminder that even in the face of adversity, courage, perseverance, and conviction can lead to greatness.
